about.lead: This application presents the Swiss registry of plant protection products. All data is fetched directly from the Confederation's linked data service on every visit; the application keeps no copy of its own.

note.duplicates: A few terms are described twice in the graph under different identifiers, among them six hazard statements and thirty application comments. They are folded into one term, and filtering on it finds the products of both identifiers.
note.effects: The full, partial and side effect properties refine ppp:pest. A pest therefore appears under both properties and is shown only once.
note.inheritance: Sale permissions and parallel imports carry no indications of their own; they take on those of their reference product. Search and query account for this inheritance.
note.language: Code list labels exist in German, French and Italian. Where a translation is missing, German and then French are used. The 23 product types carry English names only in the graph; their translations come from this application.
note.pictograms: The hazard pictograms are the public-domain UN symbols from Wikimedia Commons, bundled with the app and addressed by their code (GHS09, for instance), since the graph references no image file. They sit on a transparent canvas. Where a code has no matching file, the code is drawn inside the hazard rhombus.
note.units: The unit of a quantitative value is taken from schema:unitText. In the graph, schema:unitCode carries a doubled namespace prefix and is only used as a fallback.

source.cache: Those queries go to the cached LINDAS endpoint, which answers a query it has already seen from its store instead of evaluating it again. The registry is republished at most once a day, so a cached answer is as current as a freshly computed one and arrives considerably faster.
source.intro: Every figure in this application is read at run time from LINDAS, the Confederation's linked data service, by SPARQL queries sent straight from the browser. The application has no back end and no database of its own; the named graph below is its entire source, and the data model describes how that graph is shaped.
